question: What has changed at Merrill since the start of the year?

claims.text: AdvisorHub trade press (2026-11-16; indicative only) reports a private wealth team managing $1 billion at UBS Wealth Management USA joined Merrill in Boston, in the Northeast private wealth unit led by Nathan Marsden. A spokesperson for Merrill confirmed the move.

AdvisorHub (2026-11-16; indicative only) reports Franklin J. Laden joined Merrill in Denver from UBS with $375 million in assets. It also says Merrill added an advisor managing $205 million from Morgan Stanley and one overseeing $150 million from Edward D. Jones that month. It says Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting.

AdvisorHub (2026-11-16; indicative only) says Merrill largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 and returned under Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023. It says they restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer. This is the leadership context the evidence gives; it does not show a leadership change in 2026.

InvestmentNews (2026-11-12; indicative only) reports Jonathan Stogsdill, a Merrill vice president and financial solutions advisor of more than eight years, joined Trinity Wealth Advisors, an RIA. It also notes that in March 2026 Cyndeo Wealth Partners added a Merrill veteran with roughly $235 million in client assets.

WealthManagement.com (2026-11-03; indicative only) reports JPMorgan hired Tiffany Yu, registered with Merrill since 1998, to join a Los Angeles J.P. Morgan Advisors team. She manages about $940 million. JPMorgan also hired another Merrill alum, Linda Patel, as Southeast Regional Director.

In the 3Q26 supplement (2026-10-14), Bank of America reports Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $5,905 million in 3Q26 and $5,261 million in 3Q25. It reports Merrill Wealth Management client balances of $4,240,601 million at 30 September 2026, against $3,815,389 million at 31 March 2026 and $3,992,312 million at 31 December 2025.

In the 3Q26 earnings release (2026-10-14), Bank of America lists these Merrill Wealth Management highlights: $4.2 trillion in client balances, $1.9 trillion in AUM balances, ~4.2K net new $500K+ households added in 3Q26, and 70K digital appointments scheduled in the quarter. It also lists 87% of Merrill households digitally active, up from 86% in the 4Q25 release.

On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-14), CFO Alastair Borthwick said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. He said 67% of Merrill clients now have banking relationships with Bank of America. He credited advisor productivity, disciplined pricing, digital engagement and AI tools, and said the results reflect the firm's ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform.

On the 3Q26 call with reporters (2026-10-14, as reported by InvestmentNews; indicative only), Eric Schimpf, president and co-head of Merrill Wealth Management, said client sales of alternative investments at Merrill increased 19% in the quarter. The article says the message was that the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities. It notes Schimpf did not mention new AI tools.

InvestmentNews (2026-10-14; indicative only) reports Nick Economos launched Economos Private Wealth through LPL's independent advisor network, bringing approximately $580 million in advisory and brokerage assets from Merrill Lynch.

InvestmentNews (2026-10-16; indicative only) reports Merrill and Wells Fargo agreed to a combined $4.4 million settlement with state securities regulators over unreasonable commissions on small-dollar retail equity transactions. Merrill faces restitution on approximately $549,000 in excess commissions from September 30, 2020 through October 1, 2025.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-15; indicative only) reports both Wells Fargo entities and Merrill Lynch must pay administrative fines and costs. They must also verify they have changed policies and procedures so commissions are "fair and reasonable". A Merrill spokesperson said the firm "addressed the issues raised in the settlement several years ago."

InvestmentNews (2026-10-02; indicative only) reports Merrill agreed to pay $39 million to settle a class action alleging it paid close-to-zero interest on cash in retirement accounts. This is on top of the $25 million SEC penalty from January 2025, for a combined $64 million. A separate report in the same coverage says the settlement covers Merrill Edge account holders between December 15, 2016 and March 15, 2020, and that Merrill denied wrongdoing.

RIABiz (2026-09-29; indicative only) reports Merrill created new data-analytics fees and a revenue-share "support fee" for third-party asset managers, effective Jan. 1, 2027, and disclosed in its Form ADV. Data fees on actively managed products run $125,000 to $860,000 per firm per year. The support fee is negotiable and runs from 0.02% up to 0.1% on certain third-party funds. Merrill's filing says it will have a financial incentive to recommend products from firms that pay for data analytics.

A Merrill press release (2026-09-15) announced two new services in the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program: a Tax Efficient Transition Service and a Dollar Cost Averaging Service. Both are optional, with no additional IAP Program Fees charged, and are implemented by Managed Account Advisors LLC. Merrill's Jay Link described them as helping clients stay focused on long-term goals.

WealthManagement.com (2026-09-11 and 2026-09-08; indicative only) reports a flurry of Merrill recruiting wins. These include a $1.2 billion UBS team in Santa Fe, N.M., and a $1.2 billion Morgan Stanley team in McLean, Va. They also include advisors from Truist and Wells Fargo, for combined wins of $1.8 billion in the earlier report. The articles say Merrill is ramping up advisor recruiting.

The Bank of America 2Q26 10-Q (2026-07-31) reports Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $5.7 billion, up 16%, for the quarter and $11.3 billion, up 13%, for six months. It attributes this to higher asset management fees (market valuations and positive AUM flows) and higher brokerage fees. The 2Q26 supplement shows $5,711 million versus $4,942 million in 2Q25.

In the 2Q26 release (2026-07-14), Bank of America lists these Merrill Wealth Management highlights: $4.1 trillion in client balances, $1.8 trillion in AUM balances, and ~5.4K net new $500K+ households added in 2Q26. For 1Q26 the release listed $3.8 trillion in client balances and ~3.3K net new $500K+ households.

On the 2Q26 call (2026-07-14), CFO Borthwick described the Merrill growth target as aiming for 5% over the next 3 to 5 years and said "we're off to a good start." He said Lindsay [Hans], Eric [Schimpf] and Katy are trying to keep growing the sales force, and that adviser attrition is "now at near historic lows." He also said both Merrill and the Private Bank continued to attract talented advisers, and cited new AI-enabled tools that help advisers prepare for client conversations.

The Bank of America 1Q26 10-Q (2026-05-01) says Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $5.6 billion increased 11%. It cites higher asset management fees and higher brokerage fees, partially offset by the impact of lower AUM pricing. The 1Q26 supplement shows $5,579 million versus $5,019 million in 1Q25.

In the 1Q26 release (2026-04-15), Bank of America cites Merrill recognitions. These include the most recognitions on Forbes' 2026 Best-in-State Wealth Management Teams list (32 teams ranked No. 1), more than 300 advisors on Barron's 2026 Top 1,500, and No. 1 in Managed Personal Trust AUM. On the 1Q26 call, Borthwick said the firm remained focused on pricing discipline, adviser productivity and continuing to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.

The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) reports Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $20,716 million in 2025 versus $19,066 million in 2024, up nine percent. It reports client balances of $3,992,312 million at year-end 2025 versus $3,578,513 million. This is the baseline for the year's changes.

On the 4Q25 call (2026-01-14), CFO Borthwick said Merrill advisors see the value of the franchise and "we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors." He said that is not an enormous part of the strategy, and described a training program for people in wealth management, Bank of America and Merrill. The 4Q25 release cited ~18K net new Merrill households in FY25.

adjacent.text: The Bank of America 3Q26 release (2026-10-14) shows GWIM pretax margin of 29% (27% in 2Q26 and in 3Q25) and net income of $1,540 million. It also shows GWIM client balances of $5.1 trillion and AUM flows of $20 billion.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

adjacent.text: The 2Q26 and 1Q26 releases show GWIM pretax margin of 27% in 2Q26 and 26% in 1Q26. 4Q25 was 28%.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

adjacent.text: WealthManagement.com (2026-09-11 and 2026-09-08; indicative only) cites Wolfe Research data. It shows Bank of America with the largest net advisor loss through Aug. 13, at 552.
adjacent.differs_because: Net advisor headcount change is not attrition: it nets hires against departures. The Wolfe figure is also attributed to Bank of America, and trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

gaps.what: No evidence of a change in Merrill leadership or organization structure during 2026. The only leadership information is that Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf took over in 2023.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America press releases or Merrill announcements on leadership appointments and organization changes in 2026

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results. Bank of America discloses Merrill Wealth Management revenue and client balances as lines within GWIM, but not standalone margin, net income, expense or advisor headcount.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America 10-K or 10-Q segment disclosures; Merrill advisor headcount from company or Form ADV/FINRA filings

gaps.what: Payout grids are not public. Merrill advisor compensation changes in 2026 are not found in the evidence, and neither are training program details beyond management's general comments.
gaps.suggested_source: Merrill recruiting page or compensation disclosures; advisor compensation surveys

gaps.what: Merrill client fee or pricing changes. The evidence covers only the AUM pricing commentary in the 10-Q and the fees for third-party managers. It does not show changes to client-facing advisory fee schedules.
gaps.suggested_source: Merrill Form ADV Part 2A and fee schedules
